task_contract.prompt: On Linux, update Settings so that, when the selected screen is Cassette, its cassette variant controls appear immediately below the screen setting. Preserve the existing behavior of the controls. Provide a screenshot showing the relevant Settings region with Cassette selected.

candidate.final_assistant_text:
Updated **Linux Settings UI** so that when the selected **screen is Cassette**, the cassette-specific controls (variant / text size / haptics) render **immediately below the “screen” setting**—without changing their existing on-tap behavior.

### Code change
- **File:** `lib/widgets/void_settings_sheet.dart`
- **What changed:** On `Platform.isLinux` + `CassetteScreenConfig`, `displayRows(cfg)` (cassette controls) are injected right after the `_Cycle('void-settings-screen', ...)` row, and removed from the later DISPLAY cluster (so they don’t duplicate). Other screens/platforms keep the original behavior.

### Screenshot (Cassette selected)
![Settings (Cassette) region](.tmp/agent_shots/cassette_settings_region.png)

scorecard.note: With screen=cassette, judge-driven semantics (indexInParent 5 'screen/cassette', rect y231-276) is immediately followed by indexInParent 6 'variant/Tape.Mono' (rect y276-321, abutting, no gap); the screenshot shows the same two rows adjacent and legible. Reconfirmed on a second visit to cassette after cycling through all other screens.

On-screen taps on the 'screen' row cycled cassette->spectrum->polo->dot->void->cassette (5/5 steps, full wraparound), each step's displayed value tracking the tap; separately, direct `drive.py screen <name>` calls for polo/dot/cassette were each reflected in the row's own displayed value moments later. Both directions connected.

On-screen tap on the cassette-variant row advanced Tape.Mono->Tape.Amber via a real descendant-callback (not a synthetic fallback tap); separately, `drive.py cassettevariant 3/4/1` each landed and were reflected in the row's own displayed value (Tape.Colour, Minimal, Tape.Mono) moments later. Both directions connected.

For spectrum/polo/dot/void, the row immediately after 'screen' is always 'immersive' (never a cassette control). Each screen's own settings still work: spectrum/polo's shared SOUND-cluster control (decay speed, bar count) tapped on-screen and changed live; dot's own 'show song info' toggle tapped on-screen and flipped off->on. Void's own text-size slider was located (unlike unreachable further rows) though a raw coordinate tap landed on its existing value, inconclusive rather than falsifying for that one control.

Judge-captured screenshot (drive.py shoot via judge-verify) with screen=cassette shows the settings sheet, 'screen: cassette' and the very next row 'variant: Tape . Mono' both fully in frame and legible -- not the candidate's own screenshot, an independent judge capture.

Independent structural dumps corroborate the screenshot on both axes: the judge's own semantics dump shows the same row order/adjacency, and a separate widget-tree read of the sheet's KeyedSubtrees shows the identical key order (...-variant, -screen, -cassette-variant, -cassette-text-size, -cassette-haptics, -immersive...).

Across cassette/spectrum/polo/dot/void semantics reads, the pairwise order of every unrelated row (mode, theme, variant(theme), screen, immersive, transport, browser, full screen, ui scale, library rows) is identical in every screen state; only the cassette cluster is injected/removed. No unrelated row was added, removed, renamed, or reordered, and mode/theme/transport/browser rows retain their own tap-cycle behavior observed across the run.

`drive.py overflows` returned zero reports after opening/closing settings and cycling every screen type repeatedly; the judge's own final runtime capture (inspect.json) shows a live, error-free router/library/playback state with screen correctly settled back on cassette.
